articles.title: Dan’s Daily: Trade Demands Fizzling; Penguins Clean Up
articles.summary: The Pittsburgh Penguins played a professional, clean game Saturday, which might not normally make headlines, but after the last 10 […]
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Penguins played a professional, clean game Saturday, which might not normally make headlines, but after the last 10 periods, the choir of angels sang, and the rainbox arched the arena. The Penguins beat the Dallas Stars in a shootout, but it was how they got there that was the story, and we've got the inside analysis. Elsewhere in the Daily, the fallout is just beginning in New York, where super goalie Igor Shesterkin is out for the year.

Also, the NHL trade rumors are beginning to turn from interested teams to staying put as the players who have demanded out confront the possibility that no trade is coming. But leave it to Montreal, which tried to change that for Dylan Larkin Saturday. Those glorious hockey-loving fans chanted, "We Want Larkin!" as the Montreal Canadiens beat the Detroit Red Wings.

I didn't write about this last night. I gave it only a passing reference, but the win over Dallas cannot be overstated. This season was beginning to teeter, and another bad loss or two and they would have been in the swamp. The Penguins are far from out of the woods, but simply not beating themselves to a pulp worked wonders.

But they always play well against the larger Dallas team that doesn't play a fast brand of hockey. They've got Chicago, Colorado, Vegas, and Utah on the docket next…

If anybody wants to grab dinner at Herbs and Rye in Vegas, or Bautista's Hole in the Wall, I'm in.

Pittsburgh Hockey Now: Dan made a mistake Saturday and checked the wrong button, so this story was behind the paywall for a bit, but I wanted to make it a free PHN+ preview. It's free now—our weekly Penguins insider column. The conversations we have in the room, the chats away from the media scrums, and the vibes were getting. This week, we followed up on our deep conversation with Ville Koivunen from last season, and Evgeni Malkin interrupted a conversation to declare who he wants to play with, which is definitely a PHN exclusive. Check it out—the Penguins Room feature .

I hope many of you will come back to PHN+ now that the tech side is settled.

To the game, you can get the game synopsis and the goals breakdown here . In the report card, we dug into the Xs and Os of the contest, as well as the sad, but one immutable fact as coach Dan Muse made a couple of lineup tweaks that paid big…BIG dividends in the Penguins' win .

We also talked with Spencer Stastney after the game. Boy, he's a talker. And our postgame video. Now more concise!

NHL Trade Talk, News, & National Hockey Now

Montreal Hockey Now: We want Larkin! The fans chanted, and even Larkin was a little taken aback by the fans. What's the reality of the Montreal Canadiens' trade pursuit of Larkin?

HNIC: The Hockey Night in Canada Headlines Segment. Elliotte Friedman poo-pooed immediate speculation that the Rangers could chase Connor Hellebuyck following Igor Shesterkin's season-ending injury. Friedman also raised the possibility that a few players will remain with their teams, especially Alexander Nikishin .

NHLtraderumors.me: Friedman reported Detroit is still trying to keep Simon Edvinsson, but if they do trade him, perhaps that's the way they get the young center they want. There are four potential targets if Detroit can trade Edvinsson for a young pivot .

Philly Hockey Now: It's the middle of October, and the Philadelphia Flyers are getting worse, not better. Another–yes, another–bad loss, this time to the Boston Bruins. Our Will James has the locker room reactions and analysis from Boston. Those lovable Philly Flyers are frustrated.

Boston Hockey Now: The flip side is that the Boston Bruins are figuring it out. Jack Studley was there with good coverage of the Bruins' win .

Those two, Jack and Will, are going to be staples in this business for a long time. They're good and getting better. I'm proud to have them on the team.

Chicago Hockey Now: Frank Nazar is in timeout after his ugly hit on Bo Horvat drew a couple of game suspensions. Nazar faced the music and said he texted Horvat, too. It was a bad look for the Chicago Blackhawks forward.

articles.title: D.J. Moore: why fantasy managers should brace for "D.J. less"
articles.summary: Some teams' #1 WRs are secure atop the depth chart even when they're injured; That's not necessarily the case for D.J. Moore.
articles.body:
Some teams' #1 WRs are secure atop the depth chart even when they're injured; however long they're sidelined, these receivers will pick up where they left off. That's not necessarily the case for D.J. Moore, whose fantasy value is wobbly at best. Here's why fantasy managers should consider selling high.

Let's set the stage: Moore was a prized offseason acquisition for a Buffalo squad that needed a wideout boost. Last season, Khalil Shakir was a miscast #1, leading a group comprised of underperformer Keon Coleman, journeyman Joshua Palmer, Tyrell Shavers, and a smattering of post-prime pass catchers winding down their careers.

Compared to that group, Moore was a sizable upgrade. He then delivered big numbers in Week 1 and "sold" numbers in Week 3. Injuries limited him to only 23 offensive snaps in the Bills ' other two contests, where he caught only one pass on two targets.

Moore is not ascending. He was the Bears ' #1 WR in 2023, but by 2025 he was effectively their #3, stepping up only when Rome Odunze or Luther Burden got hurt. He'll turn 30 in April. Time isn't on his side, and neither is his current situation as an injured receiver in a corps that's getting better without him.

Essentially, when Moore finally returns to 100%, he'll be competing for targets with three guys, Shakir, Coleman, and Dalton Kincaid, who seem to have improved since last year and have, at various times this past month, looked like Josh Allen's favorite receiver.

Fantasy managers should be wary of Moore's rest-of-season value. The longer he's sidelined, the harder it will be for him to produce at a #1 WR level.

Listen to this daily podcast for the latest seven-minute fantasy takes.

articles.title: The Giants’ pass rush just lost another body it couldn’t spare
articles.summary: The Giants placed Chauncey Golston on injured reserve Saturday, turning an already confirmed absence against Washington into a larger depth […]
articles.body:
The Giants placed Chauncey Golston on injured reserve Saturday , turning an already confirmed absence against Washington into a larger depth concern. With Brian Burns also on IR, this isn't a group with much room for another unavailable defensive lineman.

The team also announced standard practice-squad elevations for outside linebacker Trace Ford and receiver Dalen Cambre. Ford adds an option for Sunday's game, but his elevation doesn't establish a permanent roster spot or a full-time replacement for Golston.

The Giants still have to replace Golston's snaps

Golston hasn't recorded a sack this season, so nobody needs to exaggerate this into the loss of the team's leading pass rusher. He played in all four games, started twice and recorded 12 combined tackles. Taking another experienced player out of the rotation still leaves work that somebody has to handle.

That work includes getting through normal downs without exhausting the remaining rushers before an important third down. A defense can miss a rotation player even when his absence doesn't remove a big number from the sack column.

I'd be careful about treating every Ford appearance as a chance to send him after the quarterback. The first standard should be a clean assignment: maintain the edge, understand the call and avoid giving Washington an easy route outside because a young player chased pressure too aggressively. More responsibility can follow reliable snaps.

An elevation helps, but it doesn't settle the rotation

Abdul Carter and Kayvon Thibodeaux remain active options on the outside. The coaching staff can ask more of established players, but asking them to carry every important snap is a different plan from having useful relief available.

The alternative is a tighter rotation, with the most trusted players handling the difficult situations and Ford contributing selectively. That might be the right approach Sunday. It also makes efficiency on the earlier downs more important because extra possessions create extra work for an already reduced group.

There is no reported return date for Golston in the Saturday transaction announcement. His move to IR shouldn't be described as proof that his season is over, and Ford's elevation shouldn't be sold as a solution before he plays.

Sunday gives the Giants a chance to see which reserve assignments they can trust. That evaluation needs to be useful beyond this one game, because a healthy Burns-Golston rotation is no longer available to fall back on.

articles.title: Mets Morning News: Guardians move on
articles.summary: Your Sunday morning dose of Mets and Major League Baseball news, notes, and link
articles.body:
Danny Abriano asked whether the Mets should bring back Ronny Mauricio in 2027.

Mets prospect Peyton Prescott has something to prove in the Arizona Fall League this season.

Despite making virtually all their players available for a potential Tarik Skubal trade, the Braves were unwilling to part with pitcher Didier Fuentes in any negotiations this past trade deadline.

Heading into the offseason, there are some questions about the Phillies' outfield that could be completely reshaped in the coming months.

Jessica Camerato listed five questions the Nationals have to answer looking ahead to the offseason.

In completely unsurprising news, the Brewers officially named Jacob Misiorowski their starter for the first game of the NLCS against the Dodgers.

Zach Sweet listed four factors that will decide the winner of this year's NLCS.

The pitching matchup of Tarik Skubal and Jacob Misiorowski is nearly unprecedented and a must-see battle in the making.

Gavin Williams tied Cleveland's postseason single-game strikeout record in last night's win against the White Sox, logging 12 strikeouts and flirting with a no-hitter.

The Guardians overcame the odds and beat the White Sox in last night's decisive Game 5, punching their ticket to face the Rays in the ALCS.

In 1969, the Mets played the first World Series game in the franchise's history—and lost.

articles.title: What Happened to Saquon Barkley? Latest Update on Eagles Star’s Injury and Why He’s Not Playing in Week 5 vs. Jaguars
articles.summary: It has been a wild turnaround for the Philadelphia Eagles over the last week. After a 2-0 start, it seemed like things were getting back on track following a...
articles.body:
It has been a wild turnaround for the Philadelphia Eagles over the last week. After a 2-0 start, it seemed like things were getting back on track following a disappointing 2025 campaign. But since then, it's gone a bit downhill.

However, it could get worse before it gets better as they take on the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 5 for their international game scheduled in London. Saquon Barkley, however, will play no part in the proceedings.

The decision to bring Barkley to town proved to be instantly beneficial for the Eagles. Setting the all-time single-season record for rushing yards (regular season and playoffs combined) was critical en route to the franchise's second Super Bowl championship.

Since then, though, the returns have been diminishing. After a mediocre 2025 season, he made a slow start this year, tallying 182 rushing yards in four games, though he left the last game against the Rams after just two carries. He will not get a chance to add to that tally in Week 5.

After suffering a hamstring injury against the Los Angeles Rams in Week 4, he was unable to practice throughout the week. As a result, he has been ruled out for their game in London.

Eagles' Outlook After Saquon Barkley's Injury

Losing a game to the Chicago Bears, who were starting Case Keenum at quarterback, was the start of this string of bad luck for the Eagles. They followed up that disaster by blowing a 10-point lead to the Rams in the final eight minutes of the game.

Moreover, Jalen Hurts finished with 93 passing yards on 27 attempts in that game, one of the worst performances of his career. But things took a turn for the worse over the course of the week.

PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN's Free NFL Playoff Predictor

Franchise legend Lane Johnson unexpectedly announced his retirement, leaving the Eagles without a key piece of their offensive line. Thereafter, in a move that many perceived as a sign that a fire sale might be in the works, they chose to trade Cam Jurgens to the Baltimore Ravens.

Now, as they face a red-hot Jaguars team, the offense appears to be in disarray. Alongside Barkley, backup running back Tank Bigsby was also placed on the injured reserve list, leaving the ground game in the hands of Will Shipley and Dameon Pierce. Carson Steele has also been elevated from the practice squad as insurance.

DeVonta Smith and Hollywood Brown have also been ruled out, leaving their wide receiver room shorthanded as well.

articles.title: Eagles edge rusher Jonathan Greenard won't play vs. Jaguars in London because of ankle injury
articles.summary: LONDON (AP) — Eagles edge rusher Jonathan Greenard won't play against the Jacksonville Jaguars on Sunday at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium because of an ankle inj...
articles.body:
LONDON (AP) — Eagles edge rusher Jonathan Greenard won't play against the Jacksonville Jaguars on Sunday at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium because of an ankle injury.

Greenard, injured in the third quarter against the Los Angeles Rams last week, did not practice this week and had been listed as questionable.

Philadelphia had previously ruled out RB Saquon Barkley (hamstring), WR DeVonta Smith (hamstring), C Drew Kendall (knee), S Marcus Epps (groin) and WR Marquise Brown (ankle).

On Saturday, the Eagles elevated TE Zach Ertz and T John Ojukwu.

For the Jaguars, S Eric Murray (concussion) won't play. He had been limited in practice. DB Jaylon Jones (hamstring) had been ruled out Friday.

The Jags' other inactives were: WR CJ Williams, CB Alijah Huzzie, OL Daniel Faalele, DE Wesley Williams, and DT Albert Regis.

On Saturday, Jacksonville signed LB Jalen McLeod to the active roster from the practice squad, elevated CB Jabbar Muhammad and S Kaevon Merriweather to the active roster from the practice squad, and waived LB Jack Kiser.

articles.title: Is Jayden Daniels playing today? Update on Commanders QB's injured elbow
articles.summary: Commanders QB Jayden Daniels dislocated his left elbow during Week 2, but got positive news this week prior to facing the New York Giants.
articles.body:
Jayden Daniels is officially back for the Washington Commanders , head coach Dan Quinn confirmed on Friday, Oct. 9.

Daniels dislocated his left elbow during the team's Week 2 loss to the Dallas Cowboys. While many anticipated the injury – which was an aggravation of an injury he suffered during the 2025 campaign – would sideline Daniels long-term, the 25-year-old has made a speedy recovery.

Quinn was asked about the value of getting his starting QB back for a Week 5 game against the New York Giants .

"Command at the line, that's one for sure," Quinn said. "The play-making ability, the third and fourth downs, all of those are part of what makes him special in that way. Love the accuracy that he throws with and the good job obviously taking care of the ball. That's going to be premium in this game."

Here's what to know about Daniels' injury , his status and Washington's overall health at the quarterback position entering Week 5.

NFL Week 4 highlights, reactions and biggest moments around the league

Is Jayden Daniels playing against the Giants?

Commanders offensive coordinator David Blough effectively announced Daniels would be playing in Week 5 during a media availability on Thursday, Oct. 8.

"He's full go, man," Blough told reporters when asked about Daniels' status. "We're looking forward to having him back."

Daniels is expected to wear a brace on his non-throwing elbow to protect and stabilize it.

Daniels' return to the lineup won't be the only shake-up for Washington's quarterback depth chart. The Commanders also figure to have a new backup quarterback, as Marcus Mariota aggravated an MCL sprain in his Week 4 start against the Colts.

That will position seventh-round rookie Athan Kaliakmanis to move into the backup role behind Daniels. The Rutgers product played in relief of Mariota against the Colts, completing 15 of 33 passes for 186 yards, one touchdown and one interception.

Below is a look at the state of the Commanders' quarterback depth chart entering Week 5:

It isn't clear whether the Commanders will elevate Hartman from the practice squad if Mariota can't play. The Notre Dame product is in his third season with the Commanders but has never played a regular-season snap for the team.

"We've got a lot still to figure out roster-wise," was Quinn's reply on Friday when asked about the team's plan for Hartman.

articles.title: Todd McLellan Admits Red Wings’ Off-Ice Drama Has Become a Distraction
articles.summary: Detroit Red Wings coach Todd McLellan admits Dylan Larkin and Simon Edvinsson's ongoing situations have created distractions for his team.
articles.body:
The Detroit Red Wings have enough challenges trying to win hockey games, but head coach Todd McLellan admitted Saturday night that the drama surrounding the organization has made his job even more difficult. Following Detroit's 1-0 shootout loss to the Montreal Canadiens, McLellan acknowledged that the ongoing uncertainty involving Dylan Larkin and Simon Edvinsson has created a distraction for his team.

With the Red Wings off to a disappointing 1-3-1 start, McLellan is trying to keep his players focused on hockey while two major personnel situations continue to hang over the franchise.

Feb 28, 2026; Raleigh, North Carolina, USA; Detroit Red Wings head coach Todd McLellan looks on against the Carolina Hurricanes during the third period at Lenovo Center. Mandatory Credit: James Guillory-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

Todd McLellan Admits Red Wings Are Dealing With Distractions

Speaking to reporters following Saturday's game, McLellan acknowledged the challenge of keeping his team focused amid everything happening outside the locker room.

As reported by the Detroit Free Press , McLellan admitted:

"I'd be lying if I said everything going on wasn't a distraction, but we have a responsibility to each other to focus on what we can control and that's what we do."

McLellan also credited the players, coaches, and training staff for supporting one another and remaining committed to preparing for games despite the uncertainty surrounding the organization.

The coach's frustration became even more apparent when the conversation continued to focus on Larkin. McLellan eventually made it clear that he was tired of repeatedly addressing the situation and did not want to discuss it further.

Dylan Larkin and Simon Edvinsson Situations Continue to Loom Large

The Red Wings have spent the opening weeks of the season dealing with two significant storylines that have little to do with what happens on the ice. Larkin's offseason trade request remains unresolved, while Edvinsson's contract stalemate has left Detroit without one of its most important young defensemen.

Saturday's game provided another reminder of how difficult those distractions have become to escape. Canadiens fans repeatedly chanted "We want Larkin," turning Detroit's former captain into one of the biggest storylines of the night despite neither team scoring during regulation or overtime.

Despite the outside noise, McLellan's team delivered a much-improved defensive performance against Montreal. Goaltender Daniil Tarasov stopped all 30 shots he faced before the Red Wings ultimately fell in the shootout.

McLellan deserves credit for acknowledging the situation rather than pretending everything is business as usual. However, the reality is that neither the Larkin situation nor Edvinsson's contract uncertainty appears likely to disappear simply because the Red Wings want to focus on hockey.

Detroit has now lost four of its first five games, and another slow start is the last thing this franchise needs following 10 consecutive seasons without a playoff appearance. The challenge for McLellan is finding a way to keep his locker room united while the organization works through decisions that could significantly impact its future.

articles.title: OVC Preview Series: Lindenwood Lions
articles.summary: Kyle Gerdeman needed to replace everyone after having the school’s best season at Division I
articles.body:
It's always difficult to replace your best player. It's even more difficult when you're coming off the high of the first winning season your school has had since entering Division I. It's three times more difficult when everyone from that team is gone, and it's back to square one. All of these things happened to Kyle Gerdeman during the offseason.

Surrounding this Lions roster is a clear bit of uncertainty. With every single player from last year's team electing to move out or move on , the coaching staff looks to rely on a multitude of new faces for success this season.

"The focus was just on how we rebuild our entire roster, and there was one thing that really helped do that, and that's that we finally were able to solidify a style of play [last year]," Gerdeman said. "After three years of getting through the transition of recruiting, I thought last year we finally got to the style of play that we wanted on offense. We got to the style of play we wanted on defense, and for the first time, really, we were able to really target guys that we thought were talented and fit our style of play vs. just grabbing talented guys and trying to squeeze them in, and I think that was kind of our approach to recruiting, to the transfer portal, [and] to everything was 'Let's make sure now that we can find guys that really fit what we want to do on both ends of the floor.'"

On the offensive side of the floor, Xavier Spencer looks to make an immediate impact in St. Charles for Gerdeman. The 6-foot-1 floor general averaged 11.9 points on 33.8 minutes per game for UMass Lowell and started all 33 games last season for the Riverhawks.

"What we needed was obviously some experience, and I thought he had that," Gerdeman said. "He played a ton of minutes last year at Lowell, played a big role for them. I think he can play some one, and I think he can play off the ball, and then really, [for] what we're doing in the half court, he can kind of combo it up a little bit. I think Mekhi Cooper was a great point guard for us, and I think Xavier gives us a little bit of that also, but I think he also kind of gives us a guy that can score and do more things than just a true point guard."

Other than Spencer in the backcourt, Kellen Robinson looks to return from injury to play his first collegiate basketball game for the Lions. Coming off an ACL tear the year prior, Robinson is the younger brother of former All-OVC First Teamer KK Robinson (now at New Mexico State), who had a standout year for Little Rock in 2023-24 before falling to two years of injury troubles. The younger Robinson now looks to prevent the injury bug after transferring from the Trojans. He was a standout for Bryant High School prior to college and was ranked the No. 3 prospect in the state of Arkansas after being a part of two straight state championship teams.

"When you come across a guy like Kellen, who was a redshirt freshman down there last year at Little Rock, I think everybody knew his talent," Gerdeman said. "So you know, now he's having a guy with some experience come in to kind of stabilize him a little bit at Xavier, and he's a guy that's hungry to get back on the court and who's obviously super talented."

Behind Robinson and Spencer are a slew of other guards who will look to carve out minutes: Shamiere Green (Lee College), Dom Clay (North Dakota State), Miles White (Lipscomb) and Malek Archie, who joined the team midway through last season after transferring from Tarleton State.

In the frontcourt, Gerdeman brought in length to pad the inside in Fresno State and Stetson transfers Makhan Diouf and Matar Diop, both of whom look to find a larger role at Lindenwood.

"What you get with Makhan is a guy that can play all over the place," Gerdeman said. "He's got tremendous guard skills, beyond being a forward or a four or five, so to speak. He can kind of give you that versatile guy. Matar Diop, coming from Stetson, kind of gives you that bouncy rim protector, that rim runner, that dunker spot guy."

Also coming in from Arizona Western College is Marsai Mason, who looks to be similar to what the Lions got from Jadis Jones in the past. The 6-foot-6 big man averaged 16.7 points and 9.9 rebounds on 51.4% shooting last season at the JUCO level. He looks to be a staple in the lineup along with 6-foot-11 North Macedonian big man Marko Lukanoski, who might be the best replacement for the loss of senior Milos Nenadic from last season.

"At this level it's hard to find good bigs," Gerdeman said. "Here's a high school kid coming in that has a chance to play some minutes as a freshman and do some things. When you find guys like that, I think you got to try to grab them."

articles.title: NC State takes a walloping from Wake, 38-14
articles.summary: It’s occurred to me lately that college football games are simply too long. A whole hour? Feels excessive. What if we trimmed the games down by, oh, let’s sa...
articles.body:
It's occurred to me lately that college football games are simply too long. A whole hour? Feels excessive. What if we trimmed the games down by, oh, let's say 30 minutes—wouldn't we all be a lot happier with a tidy sports outing such as that? I have to think we would.

Anyway, if you missed it, you didn't really, because you've seen it a lot before: NC State got outplayed in the second half. The Pack watched a halftime lead quickly evaporate and the margin went zooming in the other direction from there. Neither the offense nor the defense showed for the last two quarters, as State was held scoreless while Wake Forest scored four touchdowns and only punted the ball once.

State didn't score in the second quarter, either, perhaps reaching for bold new frontiers in underwhelming efforts moving forward. Let's hope not. But the Pack's ground game was basically useless from the start—not a terrible shock under the circumstances—and when every down is a passing down, that's generally going to be a problem. Unless you have an elite passing game, which NC State obviously does not.

Wake created a lot more havoc plays than it is accustomed to, stuffing nearly half of State's rushing attempts. CJ Bailey didn't throw an interception but Wake did a good job containing the pass game and forcing State to sustain drives, which it could not. Bailey threw for 243 yards but averaged just 6.2 yards per attempt. When the other team doesn't have to give you rushing attack even an ounce of respect, it's going to create problems.

Wake's rushing game wasn't a whole lot better, but it was far more effective than State throwing the ball. Gio Lopez was playing easy pitch-and-catch out there, completing almost 79% of his attempts for an average of 9.2 yards per attempt. NC State's pass defense has allowed 8+ yards per attempt and 2+ passing touchdowns in four straight games, and that is quite bad. Big capital-p Problem right there.

State's got some extra time to think about all of this and maybe get slightly healthier before going to Stanford. There are a lot of things that no amount of extra film study is going to fix, and anyway I'm getting to a point where I'm not sure I care much one way or the other.
